record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Does the Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture hold for Euler digraphs, meaning connected directed multigraphs in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree: does every such digraph with n vertices and minimum out-degree k contain a directed cycle of length at most ceil(n/k)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3 Does Conjecture 3.1 hold for Euler digraphs?
A directed multigraph is Euler if it is connected and for every vertex x ∈ V (D), d +(x) = d−(x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a directed multigraph $D=(V,E)$ an Euler digraph if $D$ is connected and every vertex $x\in V$ satisfies $d^{+}(x)=d^{-}(x)$, where $d^{+}(x)$ and $d^{-}(x)$ denote the out-degree and in-degree of $x$ respectively. Define the minimum out-degree of $D$ as $\delta^{+}(D)=\min_{x\in V}d^{+}(x)$, and the girth of $D$ as the length of a shortest directed cycle in $D$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: For every Euler digraph $D$ on $n$ vertices with minimum out-degree $k\ge 1$, $D$ contains a directed cycle of length at most $\lceil n/k\rceil$.

(This is the Caccetta–Häggkvist statement restricted to the class of Euler digraphs.)
artifact.status_search_result: The Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture remains open in general (proved only for small minimum out-degree r ≤ 5 and for r ≤ √(n/2) by Shen, and for digraphs with small independence number). No source found that resolves the conjecture specifically for the class of Euler digraphs, so this restricted version is also currently open.

status_evidence.title: Caccetta–Häggkvist Conjecture - Open Problem Garden
status_evidence.snippet: One of the most famous open problems in graph theory; proven only in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture is still open.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture for digraphs with small independence number
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the conjecture for digraphs of small independence number, not for Euler digraphs.
status_evidence.claim: Only special subclasses have been resolved; Euler digraph case not addressed.
